claims.claim: A useful error response carries a stable machine-readable error code when clients need one.
claims.actor: Assistant designing an HTTP error contract
claims.trigger: Client needs a stable error code while applying the error-handling skill
claims.exceptions: Only when clients need a code; descriptive useful-contract wording may be technique rather than an obligation.
claims.enforcement_effect: Possible conditional contract-content guidance; no executable enforcement established.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Both runs classify useful error-contract contents as descriptive rather than independently normative.
Stable safe ProblemDetails contracts do not explicitly enumerate these conditional fields.
Independent error-handling findings address cancellation status and other error mechanisms, not this conditional field. The error-contract claim is absent from its semantic action inventory.

claims.comparison_reason: General machine-readable contract stability may be achieved without a separately exposed application error code. Whether the descriptive sentence adds a conditional prescription remains open.
claims.distinguishing_behavioral_scenario: An otherwise stable safe ProblemDetails response provides status and title but no stable application error code despite a concrete client branching need.
claims.open_question: Does useful-contract descriptive guidance prescribe a separate error-code field, or is it only an illustrative elaboration of API-002?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Revisit canonical API-002 and the error-contract consumer rules in the policy-boundary and modality sweeps.

claims.exceptions: Appropriateness is unspecified; sentence is descriptive useful-contract guidance.
claims.enforcement_effect: Possible conditional response-content guidance; no enforced field requirement established.

baseline_comparisons.reason: Both runs classify useful error-contract contents as descriptive rather than independently normative.

claims.comparison_reason: Adding a correlation field to an error response is independent of choosing safe trace identifiers and propagating outbound context. Normative force and appropriateness remain unresolved.

claims.open_question: Does this descriptive sentence require response correlation under an identifiable condition, or merely suggest useful content?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Compare response-content guidance against logging and HTTP contracts in cross-artifact and modality sweeps.

claims.open_question: Is provider-based client setup a binding conditional choice, or simply an illustration within permitted Angular configurations?
claims.next_evidence_strategy: Revisit Angular baseline choice, NgModule exception and provider example in executable-trigger and modality sweeps.
